layers.note: Fills swamps, seeps and muddy stream margins in forest.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Grows in sun or the shade of swamp forest.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −7 °C, gone by −12 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −28 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −36 °C.

warmest_c.note: Cool to warm summers: warmest-month means from about 13.5 to 23.5 °C; below 11 °C summers are too short for it and above 27 °C too hot.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: It grows where the ground stays wet whatever the climate's moisture index, so only the driest climates (below about 0.1) rule it out; the site's own moisture places it.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Western skunk cabbage grows in swamps and seeps from Alaska to California and inland to Idaho (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
